analysis: The PR touches only CI test scripts (.github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py and test-threat-diagnostics.py) for the threat-review tooling. It changes no provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption or cache code, so provider-side threats (T-041, TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011) are not affected. The tests add coverage for four things. (1) Branch-conflict retry and bounded exhaustion on the state writes: a fake GitHub service with branch_version and branch_conflicts (test-threat-budget.py lines 45-89, 144-191). The tests assert that a ledger conflict never admits spending, that unknown checkpoint failures are not retried, and that diagnostics omit provider payloads. (2) Canonical context read from exact base-commit tree and blob objects (test-threat-diagnostics.py lines 19-55). The tests assert that mutable refs, symlink modes and oversized files are rejected. (3) Empty or whitespace-only analysis is rejected (lines 119-120). (4) Diagnostics record separate validated scanner and threat-model revisions and drop invalid values (lines 131-143). These tests check mitigations in the review tooling, whose implementation (threat_review.*) is not supplied. They do not prove those controls are correct. Whether the state-write retry code behaves as the tests expect needs separate review of threat_review/state.py and context.py if those files change. No regressions or new attack surface found in the supplied test-only changes.
